questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms as used in reproduction:

(i) Menstruation (ii) Ovulation (iii) Ejaculation (iv) Afterbirth. *(2, 2, 2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Menstruation** is the monthly discharge, through the vagina, of blood and the broken-down lining of the uterus (endometrium), when the ovum released has not been fertilised. It lasts about 3 to 5 days.

(ii) **Ovulation** is the release of a mature ovum (egg) from a Graafian follicle of the ovary, about the 14th day of the menstrual cycle.

(iii) **Ejaculation** is the forceful expulsion of semen (sperms and seminal fluid) from the penis, through the urethra, by the contraction of the muscles of the sperm ducts and penis, during sexual intercourse.

(iv) **Afterbirth** is the placenta, with the foetal membranes and the rest of the umbilical cord, which is expelled from the uterus through the vagina a short time after the baby is born.

questions.enonce_markdown: What are the advantages of birth control to a couple? *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any four of the following:

1. It allows the couple to **space their children**, so that the mother recovers her health and strength between pregnancies.
2. It allows the couple to **limit the size of the family** to the number of children they can feed, clothe, house and educate.
3. It **reduces the financial burden** and the stress on the family.
4. It **avoids unwanted pregnancies** and the risks of abortion.
5. It **protects the health of the mother** (too many or too close pregnancies cause anaemia and complications) and of the babies.
6. It gives the couple time for their education, work and care of the children already born.
7. Some methods (condoms) also **protect against sexually transmitted infections**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Red-green colour blindness is a recessive sex-linked trait in humans. Using N to represent the allele for normal vision and n to represent the allele for red-green colour blindness, determine the possible genotypes and phenotypes of the offspring of a man with normal vision and a woman who is a carrier of red-green colour blindness. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The gene is carried on the **X chromosome**, so the alleles are written as $X^N$ and $X^n$.

**Parents:** man with normal vision $X^N Y$ ; carrier woman $X^N X^n$.

**Gametes:** man: $X^N$ and $Y$ ; woman: $X^N$ and $X^n$.

**Punnett square:**

| | $X^N$ | $X^n$ |
|---|---|---|
| $X^N$ | $X^N X^N$ | $X^N X^n$ |
| $Y$ | $X^N Y$ | $X^n Y$ |

**Offspring:**

| Genotype | Phenotype |
|---|---|
| $X^N X^N$ | normal girl |
| $X^N X^n$ | normal girl, carrier of the allele |
| $X^N Y$ | normal boy |
| $X^n Y$ | colour-blind boy |

Ratio 1 : 1 : 1 : 1. Each child has a 1 in 4 chance of being a colour-blind boy: **all the girls have normal vision** (half of them are carriers) and **half of the boys are colour-blind**.
